hints.title: Small Alphabet Exhaustion
hints.text: The English alphabet has only 26 lowercase letters, so there are at most 26 * 26 possible character swaps.

hints.title: Frequency Map Simulation
hints.text: Count the frequency of each letter in word1 and word2.

hints.title: Single Character Swap Check
hints.text: For each pair of present characters, simulate swapping one instance between strings and test if distinct counts match.

hints.title: Swap Distinct Character Verification Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def isItPossible(self, word1: str, word2: str) -> bool:
        c1 = Counter(word1)
        c2 = Counter(word2)
        for ch1 in list(c1.keys()):
            for ch2 in list(c2.keys()):
                c1[ch1] -= 1
                if c1[ch1] == 0: del c1[ch1]
                c1[ch2] += 1
                
                c2[ch2] -= 1
                if c2[ch2] == 0: del c2[ch2]
                c2[ch1] += 1
                
                if len(c1) == len(c2):
                    return True
                    
                c1[ch2] -= 1
                if c1[ch2] == 0: del c1[ch2]
                c1[ch1] += 1
                
                c2[ch1] -= 1
                if c2[ch1] == 0: del c2[ch1]
                c2[ch2] += 1
        return False
```

complexity.notes: Frequency counting followed by at most 26 * 26 constant time swap simulations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all pairs of string indices takes O(N * M) which is too slow for 10^5 length.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) space since alphabet size is bounded by 26.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Leverages alphabet size 26 to test distinct character counts after constant swap trials.
